settings.title: Date.now()
settings.description: API for the blog and CMS of Date.now()

tables.description: Author authentication via magic link and TOTP. Also handles newsletter subscriber registration and confirmation.

customEndpoints.name: subscribe
customEndpoints.description: Sends a confirmation email to the provided address to subscribe to the newsletter.

response.message: Too many requests, please try again later

customEndpoints.name: confirm subscribe
customEndpoints.description: Confirms a subscription via the token received by email. The token is single-use and expires after a delay.

customEndpoints.name: generate author totp seed
customEndpoints.description: Generates a TOTP seed for an existing author account. Requires a valid JWT token. Useful for resetting an author's TOTP access.

customEndpoints.name: author registration
customEndpoints.description: Creates a new author account (role AUTHOR) and returns the TOTP seed to configure in an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator).

customEndpoints.name: author login
customEndpoints.description: Sends a magic link to the author's email address. The link redirects to the TOTP validation step.

response.message: Too many requests, please try again later

customEndpoints.name: TOTP login
customEndpoints.description: Validates the 6-digit TOTP code and returns an access token (SESSION, valid 30 min) and a refresh token (REFRESH, valid 30 days) to use in the Authorization header of authenticated requests.

response.message: Too many failed attempts, please try again later

customEndpoints.name: refresh token
customEndpoints.description: Exchanges a valid, non-expired refresh token for a new access token (SESSION, valid 30 min). The refresh token is rotated: a new refresh token (REFRESH, valid 30 days) is returned and supersedes the one just consumed.

tables.description: Media files (images) uploaded and automatically converted to WebP. Accessible at /uploads/media/{uuid}/image.webp.

GET-list.description: Returns the paginated list of media files.

GET-single.description: Returns a media file by its ID.

POST.description: Uploads an image. The file is automatically converted to WebP.

response.message: File too large, maximum size is 5 MB

PUT.description: Updates the alternative text of an existing media file.

DELETE.description: Deletes a media file. Fails if the file is still referenced by an issue.

response.message: Media is referenced by one or more resources and cannot be deleted

tables.description: Newsletter subscribers and authors. Authors can log in and manage issues; subscribers receive the newsletter.

customEndpoints.name: Get current user
customEndpoints.description: Returns the current user based on its session JWT auth token

customEndpoints.name: Get subscriber count
customEndpoints.description: Returns the number of subscribers of the newsletter

customEndpoints.name: Get user count
customEndpoints.description: Returns the total number of users. Use the optional `type` parameter to restrict the count to subscribers (users with a non-null subscribedAt) or authors (role = AUTHOR).

GET-list.description: Returns the paginated list of users. The totpSeed field is never exposed.

GET-single.description: Returns a user by their ID. The totpSeed field is never exposed.

POST.description: Creates a new user. To create an author with TOTP, use the /auth/register endpoint.

DELETE.description: Deletes a user. IssueAuthor associations are deleted in cascade.

tables.description: Tags used to categorize newsletter issues. Identified by their name (primary key, max 64 characters).

GET-single.description: Returns a tag by its name.

POST.description: Creates a new tag. The name is the primary key (max 64 characters) and cannot be changed after creation.

PUT.description: Updates the color of an existing tag.

DELETE.description: Deletes a tag. IssueTag associations are deleted in cascade.

tables.description: Reusable content categories used to structure an issue (e.g. 'Breaking News', 'News'). Identified by their name (primary key). Distinct from Tag: a category structures the content of an issue into sections, a tag classifies the issue itself.

GET-single.description: Returns a category by its name.

POST.description: Creates a new category. The name is the primary key (max 64 characters) and cannot be changed after creation.

PUT.description: Updates the color of an existing category.

DELETE.description: Deletes a category. IssueSection rows referencing it (and their articles) are deleted in cascade.

tables.description: Sponsors associated with newsletter issues. Identified by their name (primary key). The link specific to an issue is stored in the IssueSponsor table.

GET-single.description: Returns a sponsor by its name.

POST.description: Creates a new sponsor. The name is the primary key and cannot be changed after creation.

PUT.description: Updates the default link of an existing sponsor.

DELETE.description: Deletes a sponsor. IssueSponsor associations are deleted in cascade.

tables.description: External feeds (e.g. RSS sources or curated link feeds) that can be categorized with tags. Listing is public; creating, editing and deleting require authentication.

GET-list.description: Returns the paginated list of feeds. Public, no authentication required.

GET-single.description: Returns a feed by its ID. Public, no authentication required.

POST.description: Creates a new feed. Requires authentication.

PUT.description: Updates an existing feed. Requires authentication.

DELETE.description: Deletes a feed. Requires authentication. FeedTag associations are deleted in cascade.

tables.description: Association between a feed and a tag (FeedTag table). URI: /feed/{id}/tag. Deletions are cascaded. Listing is public; creating and deleting require authentication.

GET-list.description: Returns all tags associated with the feed. Public, no authentication required.

POST.description: Associates an existing tag with the feed. Requires authentication.

DELETE.description: Removes a tag from the feed. Requires authentication.

response.message: Feed, tag or association not found

tables.description: Newsletter issues — drafts, published, and archived. Each issue has a cover image, authors, tags, sponsors, and a structured content tree of sections (categories of curated articles, or freestanding text blocks).

GET-list.description: Returns the paginated list of issues, optionally filtered by status.

GET-single.description: Returns an issue by its ID, including its authors, tags, and sponsors.

POST.description: Creates a new issue. The slug is auto-generated from the title if not provided. The issue number must be unique. Content is managed afterwards via /issue/{id}/section and /issue/{id}/section/{sectionId}/article.

body.defaultValue:
{
	"title": "My first issue",
	"subtitle": "A great subtitle",
	"issueNumber": 1,
	"excerpt": "A short excerpt",
	"status": "DRAFT"
}

PUT.description: Updates an existing issue. All fields are required. Content sections are managed separately via /issue/{id}/section.

body.defaultValue:
{
	"title": "My first issue",
	"subtitle": "A great subtitle",
	"issueNumber": 1,
	"excerpt": "A short excerpt",
	"status": "DRAFT"
}

response.message: Issue number already in use by another issue

DELETE.description: Deletes an issue. IssueTag, IssueAuthor, and IssueSponsor associations are deleted in cascade.

customEndpoints.name: Get issue by slug
customEndpoints.description: Returns the full issue object (with authors, tags, sponsors, and content sections) by its slug instead of its numeric id. Public, no authentication required.

customEndpoints.name: Get issue count
customEndpoints.description: Returns the total number of issues. Use the optional `status` parameter to restrict the count to issues with a specific status.

customEndpoints.name: publish
customEndpoints.description: Publishes an issue and sends the newsletter to active subscribers. Sets status to PUBLISHED and records publishedAt.

tables.description: An ordered content section of an issue: either a category of curated articles, or a freestanding rich-text block. URI: /issue/{id}/section. Deletions are cascaded (including its articles). Positions are managed via append-on-create plus a dedicated /reorder endpoint — PUT never changes position or type.

GET-list.description: Returns all sections of the issue, ordered by position, each including its articles when type is CATEGORY. Public, no authentication required.

GET-single.description: Returns a section by its id, including its articles when type is CATEGORY. Public, no authentication required.

POST.description: Creates a new section, appended at the end of the issue (position is server-assigned). Body must set exactly one of categoryName (type CATEGORY, category must already exist) or textBody (type TEXT, validated content-block array). Requires authentication.

response.message: categoryName must be set (and textBody omitted) for CATEGORY sections; textBody must be set (and categoryName omitted) for TEXT sections.

PUT.description: Updates categoryName (CATEGORY sections) or textBody (TEXT sections) — matching the section's existing type. Never changes type or position. Requires authentication.

DELETE.description: Deletes a section. Its articles are deleted in cascade.

customEndpoints.name: Reorder sections
customEndpoints.description: Rewrites the position of every section of the issue to its index in the given order array. The array must contain exactly the ids currently belonging to the issue.

response.message: The 'order' array must contain exactly the ids currently in this collection.

tables.description: A curated article within an issue's CATEGORY section: a title, a source (link + blog/media name), and a rich summary (bold/italic text plus YouTube/tweet embeds; image embeds planned). URI: /issue/{id}/section/{sectionId}/article. Positions are managed via append-on-create plus a dedicated /reorder endpoint — PUT never changes position.

GET-list.description: Returns all articles of the section, ordered by position. Public, no authentication required. 404 if the section isn't a CATEGORY section.

GET-single.description: Returns an article by its id. Public, no authentication required.

POST.description: Creates a new article, appended at the end of the section (position is server-assigned). summary must be a validated content-block array. Requires authentication.

response.message: Invalid content blocks: must be a JSON array of objects with a 'type' field ('text', 'youtube', or 'tweet') and its required sub-fields.

PUT.description: Updates title, sourceName, sourceUrl and/or summary. Never changes position. Requires authentication.

customEndpoints.name: Reorder articles
customEndpoints.description: Rewrites the position of every article of the section to its index in the given order array. The array must contain exactly the ids currently belonging to the section.

response.message: The 'order' array must contain exactly the ids currently in this collection.

tables.description: Association between an issue and a tag (IssueTag table). URI: /issue/{id}/tag. Deletions are cascaded.

GET-list.description: Returns all tags associated with the issue.

POST.description: Associates an existing tag with the issue.

response.message: Tag already associated with this issue

DELETE.description: Removes a tag from the issue.

response.message: Issue, tag or association not found

tables.description: Association between an issue and an author (IssueAuthor table). URI: /issue/{id}/author. Deletions are cascaded.

GET-list.description: Returns all authors associated with the issue.

POST.description: Associates an author with the issue. The user must have the AUTHOR role.

response.message: Author already associated with this issue

DELETE.description: Removes an author from the issue.

response.message: Issue, user or association not found

tables.description: Association between an issue and a sponsor (IssueSponsor table). Each association has its own advertising link, separate from the sponsor's default link. URI: /issue/{id}/sponsor.

GET-list.description: Returns all sponsors associated with the issue, including their issue-specific link.

POST.description: Associates a sponsor with the issue using an advertising link specific to this issue.

response.message: Sponsor already associated with this issue

DELETE.description: Removes a sponsor from the issue.

response.message: Issue, sponsor or association not found

tables.description: Page view tracking per issue, identified by hashed IP to preserve reader privacy.

GET-list.description: Returns the paginated list of views, optionally filtered by issue. Requires authentication.

POST.description: Records a view for an issue. The IP is hashed server-side; no personal data is stored.
